checks.note: handle does recompute toTransfer via coachPayoutDebtService.planOffset on every attempt and routes any non-retryable CoachPayoutTransferException to HOLD (the catch comment even names TRANSFER_*_MISMATCH), but neither CoachPayoutDebtService.planOffset (can the offset change between attempts?) nor the PaymentGateway implementation's findExistingTransfer/AMOUNT_MISMATCH behavior is shown, and the finding depends on both.

matches.note: R1 describes the same CSRF: state is the public coach UUID, attacker pre-authorizes own Stripe account and lures victim to callback, redirecting payouts.
R2 identifies the silent, immediate stripeAccountId overwrite in upsertCoachStripeAccount with no notification/audit, sending pending payouts to the new account.

unmatched_reported.note: Concrete trigger: second coach linking an already-linked Stripe account hits the unique index, uncaught DataIntegrityViolationException on a browser redirect after the one-time code is spent.
Concrete trigger: PaymentGatewayException from the code exchange is uncaught, so the Stripe browser redirect shows a raw backend error instead of the stripe_error redirect path.
Concrete trigger: two concurrent first-time callbacks both pass findById and insert; the loser fails on the primary key with an unhandled error after consuming its OAuth code.
